title: goatbuilder config — schema version goatbuilder/v1
description: The repo-specific topology goatbuilder reads: components; environments (goatnets), the host sites within them (founder or joiner) and the machine classes within those; how each is converged; the promotion path a change travels; and any sovereign peerings. Everything repo-specific is data here; the model and the deploy contract (docs/design/goatbuilder.md) are the binary. Fail-closed: an unknown or malformed field is an error (ADR 1198).

then.description: preset lite: environments and promotion may be absent — the lite: block supplies them (one environment named after the goatnet, one founder site, one class core, one rung); repo and components may be absent — the checkout's own ops/goatbuilder/goatbuilder.yaml supplies them (the loader refuses a lite config that lacks them with no checkout config to take them from).

schema.description: The config's schema version. The binary ships the schema it validates against; a config written for a later version is refused, not guessed at.

preset.description: A named set of defaults an explicit field overrides. 'full' is this repository's shape: environments and promotion are required. 'lite' is the goatlite preset (ADR 1213, docs/design/goatlite.md): a first goatnet on one box, declared by the four facts of the lite: block (name, host, ssh_user, admin); environments and promotion become optional and derive from it (environment <name with - as _>, converger push-ansible, transport direct, one founder site <name> with class core, one rung), repo and components become optional, taken from the checkout's own ops/goatbuilder/goatbuilder.yaml when it has one and absent when it does not, secrets default to the env-file store, and a standup runs the LAN profile over the same fourteen phases. An explicit field always wins over a derived one.

lite.description: The goatlite preset's input: the four facts a learner writes (goatlite.md §2). Everything else the full shape asks for is derived from them (§3). Only meaningful under preset lite.

name.description: The goatnet's name: its site id is <name>, its ansible group <name with - as _>_hosts, its default zone <name>.lan.

host.description: The one box: its LAN address or hostname.

ssh_user.description: The SSH user the push converger reaches the box as.

admin.description: The first (and only) administrator's email: site_admins, the bootstrap identity.

zone.description: The goatnet's DNS zone, served by the box's LAN CoreDNS. Default <name>.lan.

disk_encryption.description: Encrypt the data disk (LUKS). Default true; false is a declared exclusion for a VM (doctrine P2).

data_disk.description: The LUKS data volume's device on the box. Default /dev/nvme0n1. Read by the renderer; the binary only validates its shape.

ssh_pubkey.description: Path to the administrator's SSH public key, seeded onto the box. Default the first ~/.ssh/id_*.pub found. Read by the renderer; the binary only validates its shape.

image_registry.description: Run goat's images from this registry instead of ghcr.io/<org>: <host>[:<port>]/<namespace>, e.g. 127.0.0.1:5000/usareur-af. Every goat image pin keeps its name and digest under this prefix; ops/recipes/local-registry/ fills the registry. Read by the renderer; default unset (ghcr.io).

internet.description: Growing out of lite (goatlite.md §6): the public zone and the cloud accounts an internet-enrollable goatnet needs. ops/scripts/goatlite-render.py renders the internet surface from it; the standup's profile becomes internet.

zone.description: The public DNS zone, served by Cloudflare (ACME DNS-01, the relay records, the enrolment apex netbird.<zone>). Never a LAN-only suffix such as .lan.

acme_email.description: Let's Encrypt's account contact. Default lite.admin.

aws_profile.description: The AWS profile the relay tier's Terraform tree and its SSM and Secrets Manager calls run under. Default lite.name; generate-relays.sh reads AWS_VAULT_PROFILE_<NAME> when it differs.

cloudflare_token_ref.description: Where the Cloudflare API token comes from, never a value: an op://, bao:// or bw:// reference under a reference store (written to .envrc.local.d/goatlite-<name>.refs), or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_<NAME>, the store key phase 7 reads (the default).

relays.description: The relays, one to four, each a name and an AWS region. Default two: a in us-east-2, b in eu-west-1.

mesh_ip.description: The box's mesh address, set after standup phase 8 enrols it; the router and mesh CoreDNS bind it.

source.description: The release source of record as owner/name, e.g. the GitHub repository that tags and builds releases.

image_namespace.description: The registry namespace images are published under, e.g. ghcr.io/<org>. Refs are always pinned by digest beneath it (contract C1).

release_source.description: The repository whose release workflow signs the goatbuilder binaries this project installs, as owner/name. `goatbuilder update` checks the SHA256SUMS signature against it. Omitted: source.

signing.description: How a published declaration is signed at the source (contract C2): intent-sign for the git-published intents, cosign for a registry-published index.

components.description: What can be built and shipped. Keys are component names.

environments.description: The goatnets a component is converged in, in no particular order; the promotion path gives the order.

path.description: The ordered stages a change travels. A stage's gates are the gates of the hop into it; the first stage is the entry and carries none.

peerings.description: Sovereign peerings: a declared relationship between one of our environments and another sovereign goatnet, run as the identical four-step process on each side (ADR 1157) — reachability over a dedicated tunnel, SPIRE-federated trust material, an agreed identity, and one dedicated edge router per partner. Recognition, never authorization.

deploy.description: How this project's machines and cloud account are reached. Optional: a value not declared here falls back to a name that belongs to no project, and a command that needs an undeclared value says so (docs/design/goatbuilder-portability.md).

aws_profile.description: The AWS profile a run uses. GOAT_AWS_PROFILE overrides it per command; undeclared, the profile is `default`.

ssh_user.description: The account a new machine is first reached as (`join-node`). Undeclared, a plan prints a placeholder and a real run refuses.

state_dir.description: Where this machine keeps the project's local state: goatnet CA keys under <state_dir>/<ca-name>/, standup logs and timings. `~` is the home directory. Undeclared: ~/.goat/state.

secrets.description: The team's declared secrets posture (ADR 1204): where the values a deploy templates are held. goat's own is 1password, references only (ADR 1186); a team adopting goat may choose a simpler store and owns that trade. GOAT_SECRET_STORE overrides it per command. Both avenues read it through ops/secrets/posture.py.

store.description: 1password, openbao, custom: references in the environment, resolved per command. sops, git-crypt: values encrypted in git. env-file: plaintext values in a gitignored 0600 file. env: values already exported.

sops_file.description: sops store: the encrypted dotenv file (default secrets.sops.env)

git_crypt_file.description: git-crypt store: the dotenv file under a git-crypt filter (default secrets/goat.env)

ref_prefix.description: reference stores: what a reference starts with (default op:// or bao://)

op_account.description: 1password store: the account op:// references resolve against (e.g. example.1password.com), pinned before any op call so it cannot prompt across every configured account. OP_ACCOUNT overrides it per command.

image_workflow.description: The CI workflow file that builds this component's image, by basename; null for an image built elsewhere and only pinned here.

var.description: The variable name a push converger sets to this component's pinned ref (the Ansible group_var today).

declared_in.description: Where this component's declaration lives in git — the source of record contract C1 and C3 read (the pins file today).

ledger.description: The name of this component's per-machine record (the deploy ledger directory under /var/lib/goat today) — contract C7's verification surface. Defaults to the component name.

converger.description: What makes actual match declared: an operator-driven Ansible push, or the on-host pull agent.

transport.description: How a push converger reaches an environment's hosts. direct = SSH over the mesh with an inventory: the routine path, minutes, open to every deployer on the environment's mesh. ssm = an SSM port-forward door through the environment's cloud mesh peer, open to every deployer with the provider credentials: bootstrap and break-glass grade — sessions idle out at about 20 minutes and long plays over it have died mid-run — used only when the operator's machine is not on the environment's mesh. The resolver always prefers the mesh when the operator is on the environment's profile; a pull converger needs no transport at all — the agent reaches out. An address on one operator's own network (Tailscale is the bad-day path of ADR 1114, never a transport) is not a value here: it is reachable from one machine, and doctor refuses an environment that has nothing else.

class.description: A machine class within a site (core, obs, breakglass, network-jump, pod, …). It may override the converger — the pull chain's unit of adoption is one class at one site.

site.description: A host site within an environment (ADR 1141's four-node baseline is one site). The first site of a goatnet is its founder — it originates the account, the CA and the declared ACL; any other is a joiner that attaches to the founder's (ADR 1084).

joins.description: For a joiner: the founder site it attaches to, by name, in the same environment.

environment.description: A goatnet. Its converger, transport and inventory are defaults every site and class inherits unless they override them. With no sites block it is one founder site.

peering_edge_reserved_udp.description: UDP ports this environment's peering edge hosts already hold, which goatbuilder federate allocate never gives a peering's tunnel or carrier and a pin may not take. Absent: [51820], NetBird's WireGuard. An environment whose edges run no mesh client may set [] (for example to keep a running peering on the role default 51820).

groups.description: The inventory groups a push converger targets for this environment (the goatnet's members in the pins today). doctor reads their group_vars to derive which environment variables each component's deploy templates, so a missing secret is named before any host is touched.

inventory.description: The inventory file under ops/ansible/ a push converger loads for this environment.

gate.description: A condition that must hold before a change enters a stage. The vocabulary is the release ladder's (ops/release/ladder.yaml hops), not a new one.

min_days.description: For a soak gate: the minimum days the change must have held on the previous stage.

stage.description: One step on the promotion path. A rung is an environment; a ring is a machine population within an environment (canary before stable); a tier is a geographic seam a change spreads along. The gate logic is the same for every kind.

environment.description: The environment this stage converges in. Required for a rung; a ring or tier names the environment it subdivides.

with.description: The partner's sovereign identifier — the short code its trust domain and ingress prefix are named by.

site.description: Which of our sites in that environment hosts the edge.

edge_class.description: The class at that site that runs the dedicated edge router for this partner (ADR 1157 step 4: one zenohd per partner, trusting only that partner's bundle).

tunnel.description: Step 1: the dedicated tunnel between the two edge hosts, on neither management plane.

trust.description: Step 2: how trust material is exchanged and refreshed. v1 knows one mechanism.

ingress_prefix.description: The key prefix the partner's data arrives under on our side, so provenance is in the name (cross-sovereign-federation.md §5.6).

offer.description: Narrows, for this partner, the release sets this party offers. The goat context's federation.toml owns them ([data] release); every entry here must be one it offers, and an entry it does not offer is refused (GB-129): local configuration narrows an agreement, never widens it. A set name X means release/X/**. Absent: every set federation.toml declares.

values.description: Pins that override allocation: the per-peering values goatbuilder federate allocate otherwise chooses and records in peering-values.yaml (docs/design/goatbuilder.md, Per-peering values). A pin is owned by this file and is never recorded; a pin that collides with another peering's value is refused.

hosts.description: The machines as the inventory reaches them: goatbuilder federate allocate renders the peering inventory from these, one inventory name per peering per machine.

deployment.description: Who writes this peering's deployment halves (the edge's goat-zenoh-edge values and the core's republisher values that are not the agreement's and not allocated). rendered: goatbuilder federate allocate renders them into peering-deployment.yml from the declaration and the site values, each from the declaration that owns it, and refuses one it cannot derive (GB-232). hand: written by hand. Absent: rendered, unless the peering already runs from hand-written files (hand group_vars of its edge group, or the hand inventory naming it); allocate then leaves it on them and says so, and declaring rendered opts it in.

federation_toml.description: Who writes this peering's federation.toml. Absent: rendered, unless the peering already runs from hand-written files (hand group_vars of its edge group, or the hand inventory naming it) or a hand-written file sits at the generated path; allocate then leaves it on them and says so, and declaring rendered opts it in. hand: written by hand. rendered: goatbuilder federate allocate writes ops/federation/<environment>/peerings/<with>/federation.toml from the environment's own ops/federation/<environment>/federation.toml (sovereign_id, term_days, cut_contact, [data], measured_mtu; [data] release narrowed by offer:) and the allocated values ([transport]). The environment's file stays the one owner of those values; a missing one is refused (GB-233).

forwarder.description: Present when a peering forwarder relays the partner to our edge (ADR 1218, docs/design/peering-forwarder.md). Allocation then gives the peering a public port on the forwarder and a carrier; the driver applies the forwarder from these values.

endpoint.description: The forwarder's public host, as the partner and our edge dial it (no port: the ports are allocated).

group.description: The inventory group the forwarder is in. Default peering_forwarders.

ansible_host.description: The forwarder's address as the inventory reaches it, for the rendered inventory.
